text:
mia: Heads-up — new bring-up for the compact reranker (v3-small-q8) shows consistent NDCG drop vs fp16 baseline on a few holdout slices. Small reproduction notes below, wondering if this is dataset formatting or quantization interaction. sam: how big is the delta and which slices? mia: overall ndcg@10 -1.8%, mrr -0.9%. Biggest hits on: short-factoid queries (<= 6 tokens) and docs that contain inline HTML or markdown. Longform slices mostly fine. :confused: luke: do you have a deterministic repro? can we isolate query vs doc formatting? maybe tokenizer boundary changes during int8 path. mia: yes ran quick A/B with only doc-normalization toggled. Results: when we strip HTML tags before tokenization, ndcg gap disappears for the short-factoid slice. anya: interesting — could be that q8 kernels handle some token combos poorly when punctuation is present. Any sample inputs? mia: pasted a representative pair: ``` query: "what year did Ada Lovelace publish?" doc_raw: "

Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) published notes in 1843.

" doc_stripped: "Ada Lovelace (1815–1852) published notes in 1843." ``` With q8 the model favors a different passage when doc_raw is used; with doc_stripped fp16 and q8 both pick the same passage. sam: can you show the eval command + metric output? helps rule out data leakage/seed issues. mia: running with the eval harness: ``` python -m eval.harness --model rerank-v3-small-q8 --holdout short-factoid --norm html_strip=false --seed 42 # ndcg@10: 0.811 # mrr: 0.632 python -m eval.harness --model rerank-fp16 --holdout short-factoid --norm html_strip=false --seed 42 # ndcg@10: 0.829 # mrr: 0.639 ``` luke: thanks. can you run the same with html_strip=true? mia: done: ``` python -m eval.harness --model rerank-v3-small-q8 --holdout short-factoid --norm html_strip=true --seed 42 # ndcg@10: 0.828 # mrr: 0.638 ``` So q8 aligns with fp16 after stripping. anya: that points to a formatting-quant interaction. Two hypotheses: tokenizer subtokens that include angle brackets create different attention patterns post-quantization, or some fused kernel in q8 mis-handles certain token id sequences. sam: do we see the same on other q8 variants (hybrid q8/fp16) or with different tokenizers? also check embedding scale — maybe embed bin alignment is different for punctuation tokens. mia: quick matrix: - q8 (baseline quant) -> gap - q8-hybrid (last-layer fp16) -> reduced gap (-0.4% ndcg) - q4f16 -> similar to q8-hybrid luke: hypothesis: earlier layers quantized cause representation mismatch for boundary tokens; hybrid last-layer fixes ranking logits. Could be safe mitigation to recommend html_strip in preprocessing for now. anya: agree. but we should also add a small smoke test in CI: sample short-factoid holdout with html and assert ndcg delta < 1% vs fp16 baseline. If it fails, flag as quality regression. mia: proposed smoke test snippet: ``` # in rerank-smoke.yaml holdouts: - short-factoid-html asserts: ndcg10_delta_vs_fp16: < 0.01 seeds: [42, 99] ``` sam: add one more: verify tokenizer parity between quant build and local fp16 tokenization (same token ids) for a small seed of examples. if token ids differ we fail fast. luke: also add an eval that compares top-k candidate passage overlap (Jaccard) between fp16 and q8; that helps triage whether ordering shifts widely or just borderline ties. anya: I can put together a quick PR to the eval harness with the two checks (tokenizer parity + ndcg smoke) and a note in the quant onboarding checklist to run html_strip profiling. mia: thanks — for immediate customer-facing mitigation I'll roll a doc-normalization preprocess in the dedicated onboarding pipeline and re-run the dedicated rollout tests. sam: do we need a deeper kernel-level investigation? assign to eng-runtime? :eyes: luke: let's escalate if the smoke tests fail consistently after stripping. For now log an incident if customer-facing traffic shows rank flips > 2% on short queries. eval-bot: run complete: rerank-smoke (short-factoid-html) against rerank-fp16 -> PASS (ndcg delta 0.008), tokenizer-parity -> FAIL (3/50 mismatches). See https://go/reports/3500000001 mia: oof tokenizer parity fail — that matches sam's thought. I'll dump token id diffs and upload. anya: good catch by eval-bot. once we have the diffs we can see whether it's a deterministic tokenization divergence (config or vocab) or quant-time token ID mapping bug. luke: thumbs-up. next steps: mia to upload token diffs + example pairs; anya to open PR for smoke tests; sam to add tokenizer parity check to the quant CI; i'll create a ticket for eng-runtime to look into low-level kernel interactions if token ids match and mismatch persists. mia: uploading diffs now — link: https://files.redwood/test-repro/3500000001/diffs.zip sam: nice. if anyone wants to pair on the token mismatch repro today ping me. anya: i'll start the PR and include the html_strip profiling instrumentation. luke: thanks all. follow-up meeting tomorrow 10am to triage next actions if needed. :calendar: mia: thanks — filing notes in the model bring-up doc.
